item.title: The Build Engineer
item.description:
Also known as the Platform Engineer / Automation Engineer / DevOps Engineer

The following is insight into these roles from Tom O’Neill, former Build Engineer at Romero Games, and currently Senior Automation & Tools Engineer at HundredStar Games.

General Sentiment/Overview
#

These roles would be considered the most adaptable and transferrable skill-sets to have when it comes to software development in general, and is the backbone of the games development process.

item.title: The Tools Programmer
item.description:
Overview
#

The Tools Programmer builds the tools that the artists, writers, and designers use to build the game.

Wait, doesn’t the game engine already do that for you? Well, yes and no. A Game Engine is a suite of tools that covers the basics of what you should need when building a game, but its impossible to make a set of tools that are tailored to suit every game being developed, and that’s where the tools programmer comes in.

item.title: The Animation Programmer
item.description:
The following is primarily input and advice from John O’Kane, a principal software engineer with years of animation programming experience, with my contributions sprinkled throughout. Enjoy.

Overview
#

An animation programmer’s primary role is to take a character (or object) design and provide the code and systems that will bring it to life.

This means a lot of talking with everyone involved:

item.title: The Multiplayer Programmer
item.description:
Overview
#

The Multiplayer Programmer’s job is to make sure the game works reliably across a network. From setting up lobbies and matchmaking, to supporting the shared experience of all players over the course of a match.

I’ve asked Peter Romanovsky, who was the Principal Multiplayer Programmer at Romero Games, to provide his insight into the role.

Pros
#

Why might a student want to pursue this role?

item.title: The Graphics Programmer
item.description:
Overview
#

The Graphics Programmer/Rendering Programmer is responsible for making the game look as good as it possibly can, while also making sure its within the performance budget for the target hardware. This involves working closely with artists to understand the target look and quality of the game, and working to find computationally cheaper solutions that still maintain that level of quality.

item.title: The Audio Programmer
item.description:
For advice on this role I reached out to Joseph Greaney, Senior Audio Programmer at Black Shamrock. The following is his insight and advice on Audio Programming for Games.

What is a Game Audio Programmer?
#

When a sound plays we need to know “What Why When Where and How?”

A sound designer might say, “A splash sound plays at the player’s foot when they step into a puddle.” Our job is to make sure it works as expected.

item.title: The AI Programmer
item.description:
Overview
#

The Role of an AI Programmer is to work closely with Design and Animation to breathe life into characters that make the world come alive.

Not to be confused with LLMs or Gen-AI.

To achieve this, an AI Programmer will develop systems for Enemies, Allies, and other NPCs (Collectively, “Agents”). The game will often need systems for:

item.title: The UI Programmer
item.description:
Overview
#

The UI Programmer works closely with Design and UI Artists, and is responsible for any and all user interfaces seen in the game. This can include,

  • Start Screen and start game flow
  • Settings Screens
  • The Player HUD
  • Weapon reticules
  • Enemy, Item Indicators
  • Inventory Screens
  • Minimaps
  • Quest/Mission logs

And any other screens or widgets you can think of.

item.title: The Gameplay Programmer
item.description:
Overview
#

The Gameplay Programmer is the “Swiss Army Knife” of Game Dev Engineering Roles. While other roles keep to a specialization, the gameplay programmer is defined by its lack of specialization, opting to go wide over deep to bring the other pieces together.

As a Gameplay Programmer, you could find yourself working on,

  • Player Movement
  • Abilities
  • Tutorial Systems
  • Quest Systems
  • Combat Systems
  • Game Economy Systems
  • Inventory Systems, Weapons and Items

Just to name a few.

item.title: Engineering Roles in Game Dev
item.description:
Getting into Game Development
#

I was approached to do a student talk at the University of Limerick for students of the Games Development course. For context, it’s a computer science/engineering course with a focus on games development. I’m an alumni myself, graduating in 2019, and have been working in games since then.

I asked myself what kind of advice I would give my past self when starting on this road. There’s a mountain of skills to learn, technical skills, time management, collaboration, and more. As a student you’re relying on the course structure and modules to provide you with the direction you need, but as great as the course was, for me it was missing one thing.

item.title: Hello World
item.description:
Welcome to the site! This is something I should have put together a while ago, but better late than never.

While in typical personal website fashion I’m going to be using this to showcase and link to projects I’ve worked on, I’ll also be using this as a resource for supporting my own (and hopefully others’) game development projects and personal growth.

I’ve appreciated and made use of many a game developer’s personal efforts in documenting and providing resources for game development (highlighting Ben UI’s website and Tranek’s GAS Documentation) and figured it’s time I give back.

item.title: About
item.description:
Hi, I’m Dave Ryley. I’m building tools for game development and making my own games.

I was previously Senior Gameplay Programmer at Romero Games, where I had the privilege of working with industry legends Brenda and John Romero on multiple titles for console and PC.

I love collaborating with people, and digging into new ways to support artists, writers and designers.

I have a BSc Degree in Computer Science from the University of Limerick, where I was on the team that won both the annual Robocode competition and the university’s first trophy for the National Games Fleadh.

item.title: Game Jams
item.description:
Global Game Jam 2026: Mask

Robo-Therapy: Now with 4D Emotion!

In the far dystopian future, a trainee robot 🤖 uses MASKS to navigate a therapy session with his human client. Pick the right MASK to guide your huuuman to their root cause and form a DIAGNOSIS!
Galway GJ 23: Blink and you’ll miss it.

B.L.I.N.K

You are B.L.I.N.K, a plucky robot sent to terraform alien planets to make them habitable for the arrival of the humans. There is one problem - you can only make a certain number of moves per century before having to recharge. Use your tactical skill to set up chains of events to make progression throughout the centuries possible.
Galway GJ 16: Functional Magic

Parcel Magic

Move parcels with your powerful sorcery!! What other amazing abilities will you unlock as you LEVEL UP!
Stay Safe Jam

Solitaridy

In this game you play a white blood cell taking on waves of COVID-19. If you die and start over, the ghost of your previous play-through will join you in Solidarity. This game was made by David Ryley and David Ryan in 1 day while both self-isolating in Galway, Ireland and Düsseldorf, Germany respectively.
Galway GJ 10: Extinction

Race to Extinction

Play local co-op as Space-Trump or Space-Kim Jong Un as you attempt to nuke each other’s planets.
Galway GJ 9: Anthropomorphism

Anthropomorfighters

Battle your friends with crazy hot swapping action! Is your body running low on health? No bother! Just switch to a new object!
UL Game Jam 2: Simplicity

Jam: The Game

Battle your friends to eat the most amount of Jam!
Galway GJ 9: Resist

Xal Trogg's Mighty War Bubble

You are a minor fleet commander in Xal Trogg’s mighty stellar armada and you are tasked with preparing minor world ZX-97B for liberation from the material plane. However, the inhabitants don’t share Xal Trogg’s mighty vision and plan to RESIST. Our mighty WAR BUBBLE is inbound and you must keep the populace under control! If they grow too strong they will pose a threat to the WAR BUBBLE, this we cannot allow. Tap on your STAR SAUCERS to level the dwellings of the planet, but be vigilant, as the populace will attempt to rebuild.
1GAM May 2017

Barf Royale

Royal Taster Simulator game for Mobile I created with Ian Dunbar and John Romero for the ‘One Game A Month’ (1GAM) challenge in May, 2017.
Galway GJ 7: Charge

Battleknights Go!

Power up and CHARGE your opponent.
Galway GJ 6: Rewrite History

The Bladder of Britain

Defend London against the Nazi Bombers. Created with Shane O’Malley and Dave Ryan.
Galway GJ 5: Warp

Bob's Time Adventure

Travel through 3 different ages in time to progress through the game. Created in a team of 4 at Galway Game Jam 5 in April, 2016.
